target.title: improve(gateway): reduce startup work before readiness
target.body:
Closes #105912

AI-assisted: Codex implementation and review.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup performs restart-scoped managed-plugin cleanup and loads the full worker-environment runtime before the server is ready, including on the common path with no configured or durable workers. This adds avoidable cold-start module initialization, filesystem work, and duplicate durable-record scans before the first interactive turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained managed-plugin cleanup now runs as a cancellable post-ready idle task and reuses the installed-plugin snapshot already materialized at startup. The Gateway carries one worker-environment record snapshot forward, loads the worker runtime bundle only when configured or durable records require it, and imports the protocol schema only when preparing an installation. The startup benchmark also excludes counters and memory fields from its duration ranking.

The lifecycle boundary remains explicit: cleanup waits while independent Gateway root work is active, retries later, preserves active install paths, reports failures without affecting readiness, and is cancelled during close.

## User Impact

Gateway restarts perform less work before readiness, with the largest benefit on cold starts and installations carrying managed plugin history. Dormant worker-environment support no longer imposes its full module-loading cost on every boot. No configuration, protocol, data, or plugin SDK contract changes.

## Evidence

- Focused regression suite: 68 tests passed across tooling, Gateway, and plugin shards.
- Production build: passed all `build-all` phases in 109.6 s.
- Fresh autoreview: no findings; patch correct at 0.86 confidence.
- Linux same-box cold one-shot from the initial refactor loop: 9756 ms before, 8721 ms after deferring retained-install cleanup (10.6% faster).
- Latest local five-run benchmark after one warmup:
  - default `/readyz` p50 4341 ms
  - skip-channels `/readyz` p50 4449 ms
  - 50 manifest plugins `/readyz` p50 4885 ms
- CPU profile: remaining top self-time is Node package metadata resolution, JITI module loading, filesystem open/lstat, and ESM compilation; this change avoids adding speculative caches for those broader costs.
- Import-boundary regressions verify managed-retention, worker service/live/transcript/tunnel/provider-registry, and worker protocol modules remain off the eager server import path.

Blacksmith Testbox repeatedly self-stopped immediately after warmup and direct AWS Crabbox reported the owner lease cap (`11/10`). The focused suite, build, benchmark, and CPU profile therefore used the documented local fallback. Exact-head hosted CI/Testbox and live OpenAI-on-Crabbox proof are required before merge.
